title: Count the Halogens: Mono, Di, Poly, Gem and Vic
subject: Chemistry
objective: Halogen compounds are classified first by the number of halogen atoms: one is mono, two is di, three or more is poly (tri-, tetra-). Count the halogens, not the carbons: chloroform, CHCl₃, has one carbon but three chlorines, so it is a polyhalogen compound. Dihalides split by position: both halogens on the same carbon is a gem-dihalide (alkylidene halide, e.g. ethylidene chloride, 1,1-dichloroethane); on adjacent carbons a vic-dihalide (alkylene dihalide, e.g. ethylene dichloride, 1,2-dichloroethane).

ar.a: Assertion: CHCl₃ is a polyhalogen compound. Reason: It contains three halogen atoms.
ar.r: Both true; the reason explains the assertion.

ar.a: Assertion: Ethylidene chloride is a vic-dihalide. Reason: Its two Cl atoms are on the same carbon.
ar.r: Assertion false (it is gem); reason true.

short.q: Define mono-, di- and polyhalogen compounds with an example each.
short.solution: Mono: one X (C₂H₅Cl); di: two X (ClCH₂CH₂Cl); poly: three or more (CHCl₃).
Gem: both X on the same carbon (CH₃CHCl₂); vic: on adjacent carbons (ClCH₂CH₂Cl).
